summary: I work on reliable machine learning for Earth observation. I finished an M.S. in Data Science at UMass Dartmouth in May 2026 and now work as an independent researcher.
research_interests: Reliable machine learning for Earth observation: knowing when a model’s measured skill, its explanation of failure, and its uncertainty can be trusted in places and periods it was not trained on. I find evaluation confounds that masquerade as architectural differences, test whether cross-region explanations are identifiable at all when covariate overlap is thin, and measure how well deep-learning uncertainty tracks real error under distribution shift.

research_experience.detail: Department of Computer & Information Science · Advisor: Dr. Donghui Yan
bullets: Designed a continental audit of multi-horizon urban-growth prediction: 5,698 CONUS tiles at 250 m built on Google Earth Engine, a sealed 2020 temporal holdout, and zero-shot transfer to 20 Lagos tiles (63,840 pixels).

Isolated a channel-count confound (24 → 21 input channels) that explains 94% of a CNN’s Figure-of-Merit decline at the longer horizon (delta-method 95% CI 62–100%), an effect prior work had attributed to horizon length.
Ran 1,352 MC Dropout inference runs over 8.69M pixels, showing uncertainty ranks errors reliably (r = 0.983) but understates their size by 1.4–1.9×.
Published as [1] (GeoAI 2026, oral) and [2] (Springer LNCS), with an open benchmark.
